extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent attorneys/agents, third-party requesters, and USPTO examiners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules (MPEP/37 CFR) governing ex parte reexamination proceedings: filing and timing requirements, duty of disclosure/IDS practice, interview rules, public hearings, merger/suspension of copending reexaminations, and appeals. Intended to ensure proper conduct and Office processing of reexaminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examiner’s answer limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a reply brief may not include a new ground of rejection. See 37 CFR 41.43(a)(2). A supplemental examiner’s answer, other than to respond to any new issue raised in the reply brief, is not permitted unless the reexamination proceeding has been remanded by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences for such purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference MPEP §1207.05 for supplemental examiner’s answer. Supplemental answers may only address new issues raised in the reply brief; they cannot introduce new rejections. Other supplemental answers require remand by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request timing and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant (patent owner) desires an oral hearing, appellant must file a written request for such hearing accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(3) within 2 months after the date of the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer. The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appellant will be permitted to participate in an oral hearing unless a request and the fee are submitted. See 37 CFR 41.73(b) and 41.20(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to oral hearings in reexamination and sealing petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the appeal involves reexamination proceedings, oral hearings are open to the public as observers (subject to Board admittance procedures), unless the appellant (A) petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 that the hearing not be open to the public, (B) presents sufficient reasons for such a request, (C) pays the petition fee in 37 CFR 41.20(a), and (D) the petition is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP §1209 relates to oral hearings in appeals in both patent applications and ex parte reexamination proceedings. Petition to close hearing requires sufficient reasons, fee, and grant of petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review (appeal to courts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner not satisfied with the decision of the Board may seek judicial review. For ex parte reexaminations filed before November 29, 1999, appeals could be to (A) U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141) or (B) U.S. District Court for D.C. (35 U.S.C. 145). For reexaminations filed on or after November 29, 1999, appeal is only to the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These distinctions are based on the statute amendments and Public Law changes; see Section 13202(d) of Public Law 107-273. Third party requesters may not seek judicial review, though courts may allow intervention in limited circumstances (citations provided). See MPEP §§1216, 1216.01, 1216.02 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure in reexamination (continuing duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding (patent owner, each attorney/agent representing the owner, and every other individual substantively involved on behalf of the owner) has a continuing duty of candor and good faith to disclose to the Office all information known to that individual to be material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding (applies with respect to each claim pending until the claim is cancelled).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duty is deemed satisfied if all information known to be material to patentability of any claim after issuance of the reexamination certificate was cited by the Office or submitted in an IDS. Fraud, bad faith, or intentional misconduct violates the duty. Responsibility for compliance rests on the individuals designated; Office will not evaluate compliance during the proceeding but unresolved questions will be noted per §1.552(c). See MPEP §2282 and §2686 for related duties to disclose prior/concurrent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "information material to patentability" in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material to patentability in a reexamination proceeding when it is not cumulative to information of record or being made of record, and (1) it is a patent or printed publication that establishes, by itself or in combination with other patents/printed publications, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes or is inconsistent with a position the patent owner takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office or in asserting an argument of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance of the evidence standard, giving each claim term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, and before considering evidence to establish a contrary conclusion of patentability. See 37 CFR 1.555(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filing and required copies for reexamination (37 CFR 1.98 application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information disclosure statement (IDS) must be filed with the items listed in §1.98(a) as applied to individuals associated with the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding, and should be filed within two months of the date of the order for reexamination, or as soon thereafter as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2) requires a legible copy of: (1) each foreign patent; (2) each publication or that portion which caused it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office); (3) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims and any drawing or that portion causing it to be listed; (4) all other information or that portion which caused it to be listed. The exception to the copy requirement in 1.98(d) does not apply to ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings. Copies should be supplied to comply with 1.98(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content rules for IDS submissions in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals are strongly encouraged to file IDSs in accordance with 37 CFR 1.98 within two months of the order to reexamine. An IDS filed after the order and before the first action on the merits may be submitted as part of the statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or as a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed as part of a statement under 1.530, the submission may include a discussion of patentability issues; if filed as a separate paper, it must be limited to listing the information disclosed and an explanation of its relevance — any discussion relating to patentability would be improper. An attorney/agent who receives information has no duty to submit it if it is not material to patentability per 37 CFR 1.555(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of noncompliance with duty of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fraud practiced or attempted on the Office or violation of the duty of disclosure through bad faith or intentional misconduct by any individual results in noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.555(a). Individuals who fail to comply do so at the risk of diminishing the quality and reliability of the reexamination certificate issuing from the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues of noncompliance raised during a reexamination proceeding will be noted as unresolved questions under 37 CFR 1.552(c). The duty of disclosure in reexamination proceedings is consistent with duty under 37 CFR 1.56 for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews must be in-Office and limited (37 CFR 1.560)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews between examiners and owners (or their attorneys/agents) in ex parte reexamination proceedings must be conducted in the Office during Office hours at times the examiners designate; interviews will not be permitted at other times or places without Director authority. Interviews for discussion of patentability will not be conducted prior to the first official action. Interviews should be arranged in advance; requests by reexamination requesters to participate will not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone interviews to requester to discuss filing-date noncompliance are permitted when no reexamination proceeding exists. Panel members will be present when practicable after panel review. Examiner-initiated pre-first-action interviews may be allowed only to present an amendment that makes claims patentable where the patent owner’s role is passive (only agree/not agree). Patent owner’s questions on purely procedural matters may be answered anytime; examiners must not discuss merits with third parties — refer procedural questions to CRU SPE or TC QAS. Guidelines to distinguish procedural questions (obtainable by reading file) vs merits (not available from file) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner’s written statement of the interview (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance of an interview with the examiner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding, a complete written statement by the patent owner of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed. The written statement must be filed as a separate paper within one month from the date of the interview, or as a separate part of a response to an outstanding Office action, whichever is later (37 CFR 1.560(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement cannot be waived by the examiner. Failure to file the written statement as required under 37 CFR 1.560(b) will result in termination of the reexamination prosecution (per 37 CFR 1.550(d)), similar to failure to timely respond to an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-interview submissions and interview duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner desires to initiate an interview, the owner should contact the examiner to indicate the issues and determine if an interview will be granted. If granted, the patent owner must file, at least three working days prior to the interview, an informal written statement of the issues to be discussed and an informal copy of any proposed claims to be discussed (unless examiner waives requirement). These materials should be faxed or hand-carried to the examiner to avoid delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The informal copies considered by the examiner will be made of record as an attachment to the Interview Summary form PTOL-474. The duration of the interview will not exceed one hour unless the patent owner files a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 showing sufficient cause for more time. Examiner may extend the interview at examiner’s discretion; only one interview may be requested after an Office action and prior to filing response absent showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview recordkeeping (PTOL-474)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must complete an Ex Parte Interview Summary form PTOL-474 for each interview where a matter of substance has been discussed. A copy of the form should be given to the patent owner at the conclusion of the interview; the original should be made of record in the reexamination file, and a copy should be mailed to any third party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General procedure for conducting and recording interviews is described in MPEP §§713.01-713.04. Informal interview materials considered by the examiner will be attached to PTOL-474.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.565)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination proceeding, the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (e.g., interferences, reissues, ex parte or inter partes reexaminations, or litigation) and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will accept, at any time, copies of notices of suits and other proceedings and copies of decisions or papers filed in court for entry into the reexamination file to ensure a complete file. Proper submissions will be entered and considered by the examiner when the proceeding comes up for action on the merits. Form paragraphs 22.07/22.08 may be used to remind owners of the continuing duty under 37 CFR 1.565(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on submissions regarding concurrent proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to notify the Office of prior/concurrent proceedings must be limited to bare notice (identifying application/proceeding number and status); parties must not include arguments or extensive papers. Highlighting of text or inclusion of arguments is improper and such submissions will be returned, expunged, or discarded at Office discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-merit decisions (e.g., venue, trial date, sanctions) will not be entered and will be expunged if entered in error. If volume of papers is too extensive, Office may return/expunge/discard all or part; parties should limit submissions to relevant notifications. If an IDS submitted in litigation stage is proper, it will be entered and considered on next action on merits. If submission is not permitted entry it will be returned/expunged/discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for granting second/subsequent ex parte reexamination (substantial new question of patentability)
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a second or subsequent request for ex parte reexamination to be granted while an earlier ex parte reexamination is pending, a substantial new question of patentability must be raised by the art (patents and/or printed publications) cited in the later request (see MPEP §2240 for discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If granted, the CRU Director (or delegate) will decide whether to combine proceedings. The second request should be processed quickly and assigned to the same examiner as the first; it should be decided immediately without waiting the usual period. If denied, prosecution of the first continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of copending reexamination proceedings and identical claims requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reexamination proceedings are merged, the CRU decision should require that the patent owner maintain identical claims in both files. Responses and other papers in the merged proceeding must consist of a single response, addressed to both files, filed in duplicate, each bearing a signature and identifying data for both files for entry in both files. If the claims are not the same, the merger decision will give the patent owner one month to provide an amendment to make the claims the same in each file; identical amendments are to be placed in all files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner fails to timely submit the amendment to make claims identical, any claim not identical in all merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as indefinite. Where claims already identical, prosecution continues at the most advanced point possible. A single certificate will be issued based on merged proceedings (37 CFR 1.565(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution after merger and reopening where new grounds arise
rubrics_metrics.description: If proceedings are merged, prosecution will continue at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding. If a final rejection has been issued in the first proceeding, prosecution will ordinarily be reopened where any new patents or printed publications presented in the second request are applied to the merged proceeding in a new ground of rejection. The patent owner will be provided an opportunity to respond to any new rejection in a merged proceeding prior to the action being made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first proceeding's ex parte prosecution stage had not begun when Request 2 is received, Request 1 is processed to readiness for ex parte prosecution and then normally held until Request 2 is granted; if Request 2 denied, no merger and prosecution proceeds solely on Request 1. Request 2 should be determined on its own merits and should not rely on or refer to the decision in Request 1.
